case_title: Shim Singh v. State of Uttarakhand
accused_occupation: Not stated by the court. Defence counsel said Shim Singh was a vehicle driver and Aan Singh a chowkidar in P.W.D.
accused_victim_relationship: Spouse (husband, appellant No.1); other appellants were the husband's brothers and a brother's wife (in-laws of the deceased)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.304-B; IPC s.498-A; Dowry Prohibition Act 1961 s.3 and s.4; Evidence Act s.113-A and s.113-B (presumptions)
weapon: Poison (organo chloro insecticide and ethyl alcohol found in viscera); fire (victim's body burnt)
evidence_type: Circumstantial evidence; medical evidence (autopsy and viscera chemical report); oral evidence of relatives and village head
confession: Admissions under s.313 CrPC to the marriage date and unnatural death only; not a confession of the offence; not treated as such by the court
aggravating_circumstances: Death within about five months of marriage; 90% burns; poison found in viscera; death at in-laws' house; prior complaints of dowry-related taunts and torture
trial_court_outcome: Appellants 1 and 2 convicted under s.304-B IPC (life imprisonment); all four convicted under s.498-A IPC (rigorous imprisonment; term stated as one year at p.5 and three years at p.7) and DPA ss.3-4 (three months' RI and fine); sentences concurrent
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; acquitted co-accused Nain Singh and Janki Devi; conviction and sentence of appellants 1 and 2 upheld
offence_finally_established: Dowry death under IPC s.304-B (appellants 1 and 2)
neutral_facts: The victim married the accused in May 1997. About five months later, on 26 September 1997, the victim died at the matrimonial home. The village head reported the unnatural death by telephone to the sub-divisional magistrate. The body was found with about 90% burn injuries. The accused, including the victim's husband, his brothers and his brother's wife, told the village head that the victim had set herself on fire. Post-mortem examination by two doctors could not ascertain the cause of death from external examination, so the viscera were preserved. Chemical examination of the viscera detected organo chloro insecticide and ethyl alcohol. The victim's brother, father and uncle testified that the victim had complained of taunts and torture over dowry. One witness said that at a post-marriage ceremony an accused complained that the marriage expenses had not been recovered. The victim had complained to the family twice about dowry demands. The victim's brother said no dowry demand was made before the marriage. The defence contended that the victim had swallowed poison and then set herself on fire. Police investigated, and a charge-sheet was filed against all four accused.
physical_harm: Death of the victim; 90% burn injuries (skin deep); poison found in viscera
number_of_offences: 4 charged (IPC s.304-B; IPC s.498-A; DPA s.3; DPA s.4); 4 finally upheld as to appellants 1 and 2 (appeal dismissed)
premeditation_planning: No explicit finding of premeditation; court noted only that the accused had the opportunity to administer poison
motive: Dowry demand: cruelty and harassment for dowry accepted by the court; alleged: resentment over unrecovered marriage expenses
key_evidence_accepted: Post-mortem and viscera report; oral evidence of relatives (PW-1, PW-2, PW-3) on dowry taunts and the durgun incident; victim's two prior complaints; death within five months of marriage; s.313 admissions; death in accused's house; opportunity to administer poison
witness_credibility: Court accepted the relatives' testimony on dowry demands as cogent and consistent; defence points that no dowry demand was made before marriage and no prior police report was lodged were rejected
post_offence_conduct: Accused informed the village head of the death and said the victim had set herself on fire; court found that failure to take the victim to hospital was inconsistent with innocence
trial_duration: offence: 26.9.1997; trial judgment: 25.04.2000; High Court: 23.03.2009; Supreme Court: 11.02.2015
legal_representation: Accused: Garvesh Kabra. State of Uttarakhand: Ashutosh Kr. Sharma and Abhishek Atrey
investigation_status: FIR lodged 27.9.1997; investigation by DSP; charge-sheet filed; case committed to Sessions Court; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court (25.04.2000): appellants 1 and 2 convicted under s.304-B IPC and others; High Court (23.03.2009): appeal dismissed, conviction of appellants 1 and 2 upheld, two co-accused acquitted; Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: Accused poisoned the victim after dowry-related torture, then set her on fire to ensure death and to prevent a dying declaration; victim had complained twice of dowry taunts
defence_argument: No dowry demand before marriage and no prior complaint; accused themselves reported the death; victim committed suicide by consuming poison and then self-immolation; the accused were not all involved
legal_principle_applied: Conjoint reading of s.113-B Evidence Act and s.304-B IPC: cruelty or harassment soon before death for dowry raises presumption of dowry death; alternatively s.113-A presumption of abetment of suicide; circumstantial evidence must form a complete chain; motive not essential
precedent_relied_upon: State of Himachal Pradesh v. Nikku Ram (1995) 6 SCC 219; Kaliyaperumal v. State of Tamil Nadu (2004) 9 SCC 157; Bansilal v. State of Haryana (2011) 11 SCC 359; Hemchand v. State of Haryana AIR 1995 SC 120; Gurbachan Singh v. Satpal Singh 1990 Cri LJ 562; Gurpreet Singh v. State of Haryana (2002) 8 SCC 18; Sharad Birdhichand Sardar v. State of Maharashtra (1984) 4 SCC 116; Mulakh Raj v. Satish Kumar (1992) 3 SCC 43; State of Maharashtra v. Annappa Bandu Kavatage (1979) 4 SCC 715; Kusuma Ankama Rao v. State of Andhra Pradesh (2008) 13 SCC 256
judicial_aggravating_factors: Death within five months of marriage after dowry-related cruelty; death at accused's house; victim described as healthy and reconciling with accused, so suicide was ruled out
